text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A family of three and a former Kenya Air Force Major are among the eight people who died in the Wednesday afternoon aircraft crash on Ngong, a hilly area in the suburbs of Nairobi.
- Members of Parliament from Western Kenya, meet Kenya's president privately and tell him that party secretary-general Joseph Kamotho is a liability to the party.
- President Daniel arap Moi establishes an 11-man team to develop and guide Kenya's economy with the aim of alleviating poverty.
- In yet another night of bloody terror in the crime-hit area of Kiambu district, a man is beheaded, prompting a massive search operation by the police.
- Jailed political prisoner Koigi wa Wamwere has won the "Writers in Prison" award for his publications-- 'The Dream of Freedom and A Kenyan Trial'.
- The Maendeleo Ya Wanawake Organisation (MYWO) requests the Attorney General to present a fresh bill in Parliament seeking a total ban on female circumcision.
- A 16-year-old goes to relieve herself while sitting for her final year examination only to come back with a bouncing baby boy. Not to be discouraged, she tackles her paper to the very end.

- The issue of whether or not national party Kenya African National Union, should carry out its long overdue national party elections before the next general election continues to widen the rift within the party.
- Virtually all public utility plots in the rural areas of Ndumberi and Ting'ang'a, Kiambu district have been acquired by a few individuals, who did not follow laid down procedures.
